hypotheses.reasoning: Until 08:07:31 everything was healthy (#88, #92). At 08:07:34 payment-svc-1 failed its liveness probe and restarted, dropping capacity to 3/4 (#94). order-service then retried the 503s immediately with backoff disabled (#96, #102, #108). That pushed load on payment-svc to 3.2x and then 4.1x baseline (#104, #123), so it started shedding load with 'queue full' 503s (#114, #130, #140). The gateway returned 503s after its retries ran out (#107, #111). This is a retry storm that keeps itself going, which is why errors are not recovering. Losing one instance on its own would not cause this.
Something unknown may have exhausted payment-svc-1 and caused the failed liveness probe. GC and heap readings just before look normal (#90: heap 35%).
Retry backoff is disabled in the order-service PaymentClient, which may be a misconfiguration. No config-change event appears in the logs.

verdict.recommendedAction: Break the retry storm. Turn on exponential backoff with jitter, and add a circuit breaker or retry budget to the order-service PaymentClient (or cut retries to 1 for now). Rate-limit or shed load on /checkout at the gateway until payment-svc's inflight count drains. Make sure payment-svc-1 comes back so capacity returns to 4/4, and scale payment-svc up for now. Then find out why the payment-svc-1 liveness probe failed and why backoff was disabled.
